NB: Items may vary slightly in appearance from that pictured. Please contact us if you have any questions.   Physical description The double bell gankogui is a hand-forged iron bell. One gankogui actually consists of two bells, the smaller, higher-pitched one resting atop the larger, lower one.  Many Ewe ensembles include two gankoguiwo, one much bigger than the other. History The gankogui is sometimes referred to as gakpevi, or "forged iron carrying a child". The larger bell is considered to be the parent of the smaller one. (Ladzekpo) Most good gankoguiwo are made in Togo and Benin. (Pantaleoni 1972: 58) Tuning The larger bell of the gankogui is tuned approximately one octave below the smaller one. Technique The repetitive pattern of the gankogui provides a reference point for all of the other instruments in the ensemble. The gankogui is played with a wooden stick and is held in the strong hand where the two bells are joined. The player sits upright with the bottom of the large bell resting on the thigh. There are three syllables referring to the different strokes applied to the gankogui: tin (rebounding shot on the large bell), go (rebounding shot on the small bell), and ka (shot pressly firmly into the small bell). Variations on these sounds are achieved by damping on the thigh the open bottom of the large bell. (Ladzekpo) Notation The music of the Ewe drum ensemble is transmitted almost exclusively aurally. The vocables, however, are similar to notation in that they serve as a tool for learning and remembering rhythms and patterns. Context The gankogui plays a cyclical ostinato that provides a reference point for all other instruments and dancers in the ensemble. The Ewe live between the Volta and Mono rivers in West Africa, in what is now Ghana and Togo. (Locke 1979: 01) The Ewe have migrated to this area from Benin and Western Nigeria since the 16th century. References Galeota, Joseph. 1985. "Drum Making Among the Southern Ewe People of Ghana and Togo." M.A. thesis, Wesleyan University. Locke, David. 1979. "The Music of Atsiagbeko." 2 vols. Ph.D. dissertation, Wesleyan University. Pantaleoni, Hewitt. 1972. "The Rhythm of Atsia Dance Drumming Among the Anlo (Ewe) of Anyako." Ph.D. dissertation, Wesleyan University. Author: Isaac P. Hirt-Manheimer

AFRICAN DRUM CLASSES – DJEMBE

  Our African drum classes have three groups. These are called Kalankora Foli for the beginners drum class, Badenya Foli for the intermediate drum class and Foli Kan for the experienced drum class. Foli means play in the Manding languages and play is what we are all about!!  

KALANKORA FOLI – BEGINNERS DRUM CLASS

  The beginners class is for people with little or no experience playing djembe (West African drum). It is a class that is about finding your rhythm and the three essential sounds your djembe can make to create rhythms. Playing rhythms together, we will build a vocabulary of how these sounds are arranged together to make the rhythms and songs of the djembe. After 3 or 4 months you will be ready to move on into Badenya Foli.  

BADENYA FOLI – INTERMEDIATE DRUM CLASS

  Badenya means community in the Manding languages and this class is where we begin to explore the relationships between the instruments and the rhythms they play. Just as a community is created through the relationships of its people, rhythms are created through the relationships of the instruments, the rhythms they play individually and together, and the roles they fulfill in the music.  

FOLI KAN – EXPERIENCED DRUM CLASS

  Foli Kan means literally “play sound” and in this class we begin to do just that. With the sounds, rhythms and techniques in our hands we can take our instruments and music and play with them. The rhythms and their melodies play harmoniously together creating music that we perform to the community. With breaks, songs and solos we play music that connects and celebrates people and community. Foli Kan is often joined by the Muso Foli Dance Troupe who bring the joy and spirit of African dance to the performance.

AFRO POP COMMUNITY DANCE CLASSES

 

Find your rhythm, get fit and have fun with these African inspired dance classes. Improve memory, coordination and movement to upbeat recorded music. Learn West African moves and discover rhythm. These classes are for everyone. Discover the joy of dance with the community every Saturday in Noosa.

This 4 week course presented by the Noosa Shire Council is FREE. The classes are progressive and it is recommended that you commit to the full 4 weeks to gain the maximum benefits.

Participants will need to bring water wear comfortable clothes.

Dance Classes will be held at the Tewantin State School, Werin Street,Tewantin Qld 4565.

Class Dates: September 11th, Sepetember 18th, October 9th, October 16th

Class Times: 10.30-11.30am

Would you like to learn how to drum and dance at the same time? Learn more about the Dundun Dance Class that starts at 11.30am here. 

To secure your place. please complete the enrolment form below.

Name: Dundun Dance 4 week course - Tewantin
Short description: There is also a drum hire fee which is $4.00 per week.
Description: Dundun Dance Classes are active dance classes which combine West African dance moves with West African Dundun drumming. Dunduns are played with sticks and are cylindrical in shape and double ended. They originate from West Africa. These classes will have you moving around your drum, clapping sticks, beating drums and smiling large. It is incredibly fun and you needn’t be a dancer or a drummer to do this class. It is a fantastic class for stress relief, fitness and coordination. This class helps develop an understanding of the rhythm to dance which is essential to African culture and music. If you would like to see Bec's Dundun dance class in action see here. The dates are: 11th September 11.30-12.30pm 18th September 11.30-12.30pm 9th October 11.30-12.30pm 16th October 11.30-12.30pm The classes will be held at the Tewantin State School These classes are non refundable and non transferable

Camp Afro Foli

DRUM CAMP AND DANCE CAMP 24-26 JULY 2026

Grab your tickets now!! Where: 1 Beach Rd, Noosa North Shore, QLD 4565 Noosa North Shore Retreat Sleep: Shared, spacious two bedroom apartment accommodation with kitchen, lounge room and two bathrooms, which sleep approximately 6 people per apartment. We have also added accommodation options for this years drum camp and dance camp and so if you are wanting to share with your partner, spouse, or bestie then you can. We have also added a 1 person option for those wanting there own room.  Every apartment has its own kitchen. Bedding is included, however we recommend that you bring your own bedding including pillow, doona or sleeping bag for extra warmth if you feel the cold. Every effort will be made so that friends or groups will be in apartments together, and that people with 1 person or 2 person accommodation options will be in apartments where the other room has the same option. However, while every effort will be made we cannot guarantee this. Camping options are also available this year and if you would like to camp at this years Camp Afro Foli drum camp and dance camp then please select the no accommodation option. The apartments surround a communal area and fenced pool. Eat: This is a self – catered event. Every apartment has its own kitchen with the basics including gas cook tops and oven. There is an outdoor BBQ area next to the pool with 4 BBQS to cook on. Please bring your own food and there will be a shared BBQ on the Friday night for those who would like too. There is a bistro and bar onsite for meals, snacks and drinks. Drinks: You can BYO to this event and there is also an onsite bar and bistro open throughout the camp. Please be respectful and drink responsibly. There will be lots of workshops and an artist performance on the Saturday night. Three days of movement, fun, cultural workshops and performances, with international artists bringing Africa to the Sunshine Coast. Enjoy beautiful beach surroundings, world class talent and be immersed in West African culture with workshops in djembe, dancing, dundun drumming, and dundun dancing. Loads of action to choose from and the promised gift of rhythm for your hands and feet. Read more to find out about the artists, the camp and the daily program. Terms and Conditions: All Camp Afro Foli Drum Camp and Dance Camp full camp passes are non-refundable, non-transferable, and cannot be exchanged for classes or services at a later date. Artists may be subject to change without notice due to unforeseen circumstances. Camp Afro Foli program is subject to change without notice.
